ttp-attack-mapping-reliability.rationale: LOWERED 3 -> 2. THIS IS THE ONLY SCORE THAT MOVES THIS CYCLE. It moves because ctr-0006 (opened cycle 28, resolved_cycle null) attacks the text of this issue's FIRST supported candidate, and because both legs of the candidate cycle 26 designated as the level-3 carrier are now known to lack a stated correctness rule. Nothing else has touched this issue since cycle 16 (attempts [16]). WHAT ctr-0006 ESTABLISHED AT SOURCE, verbatim and PRESENT in two independent fetches of arxiv.org/html/2406.07599v3: Section 4.2 says 'We adopt the Micro-F1 score as the evaluation metric for the CTI-ATE task' while Table 1's column header reads 'CTI-ATE (Macro-F1)'. Micro and Macro F1 are different quantities and diverge substantially over the 397-technique multi-label space CTI-ATE uses, so 0.6388's metric identity is AMBIGUOUS BY THE PAPER'S OWN TEXT and is unresolvable from the paper. The paper also NEVER STATES how a predicted ATT&CK technique is counted as correct (exact ID, parent, sub-technique, partial credit) -- ABSENT in two fetches. CANDIDATE 1 (status supported, evidence [src-0002, src-0005]) IS THE DIRECT SUBJECT OF ctr-0006 AND NOW CARRIES NOTHING. Its first sentence reads '0.6388 ... far below the ~71-72% accuracy the same models reach on knowledge-recall tasks'; the paper defines CTI-MCQ and CTI-RCM as multi-class classification accuracy against a multi-label F1, so those cannot be differenced, and exact-string checks returned 'task difficulty' ABSENT, 'most challenging' ABSENT, and a third fetch asked for every between-task comparison answered ABSENT. Its second sentence rests on src-0005, which cycle 26 established REPORTS NO ATT&CK METRIC AT ALL. So candidate 1's ATT&CK-specific content is a comparison the source's own metric definitions forbid, plus a source that does not measure the task. A T4 CANNOT REWRITE A CANDIDATE -- ctr-0006 records the path and it is a T3's job -- but I must price it as it stands. CANDIDATE 2 (evidence [src-0007, src-0002]) IS WHAT CYCLE 26 SAID CARRIED THE 3, AND I READ IT IN FULL RATHER THAN TRUSTING THAT RATIONALE. It is genuinely the better candidate: it explicitly DISCLAIMS commensurability ('different benchmark, different corpus, and a different metric decomposition'), so ctr-0006's second finding does not touch it, and its numbers are the best-verified in this base -- src-0007's nine figures verbatim to four decimals at cycle 15 with a whole-table re-pull at cycle 21, and src-0002's ChatGPT-4 row re-confirmed a third time at cycle 28 as 71.0 / 72.0 / 1.31 / 0.6388 / 52 / 86. Its two distinctive contributions are (a) INDEPENDENCE and (b) a WITHIN-TABLE CONTROL. WHY THAT IS NO LONGER A 3, TAKING BOTH IN TURN. (b) IS COMPROMISED. Candidate 2 argues that because the identical models reach 0.8240-0.8846 precision on mechanical IoC extraction in the same table, the ATT&CK deficit 'cannot be attributed to corpus difficulty or prompt harness quality'. ctr-0004 (cycle 27) read the released scorer and found the IoC side is matched by ONE-DIRECTIONAL substring containment -- the executing code is any(pred.lower() in gt.lower() for gt in gt_set), so a prediction need only be a SUBSTRING OF a ground-truth entry -- while the ATT&CK/TTP scorer in the same artefact has never been read. A control that compares a leniently scored number against an unknown-scored number is not a control. (a) DELIVERS LESS THAN CYCLE 26 CREDITED. After ctr-0006, NEITHER leg has a stated ATT&CK correctness rule, one leg's metric is ambiguous between Micro-F1 and Macro-F1 by its own paper's text, and the two magnitudes differ by more than a factor of two (0.6388 F1 against 0.2787/0.2270 precision/recall) in a way the candidate itself says cannot be reconciled. What the two independent sources jointly establish is therefore the DIRECTION of a claim -- ATT&CK technique mapping scores low -- computed under two rules neither of which is known. Level 3 asks for a primary candidate supported by two independent sources; I read 'supported' as requiring the sources to measure a determinate quantity, and per step 5's instruction to take the lower score when torn, that is a 2. WHAT DID NOT CHANGE AND MUST NOT BE STRIPPED. src-0007's nine figures stand exactly and remain the best-verified numbers in this base. Fine-tuning makes this sub-task WORSE, not better (0.2787/0.2270 GPT-4o falling to 0.2387/0.1846 fine-tuned, and 0.1771/0.1414 for fine-tuned GPT-4o-mini). src-0005's two ranges (Threat Intelligence Reasoning 'range from approximately 43%-53%', Malware Analysis 'from approximately 23-34%') are real but are all-or-nothing multi-select multiple-choice accuracies and are not commensurable with an F1 over free-form extraction, so they still do not make src-0005 a measuring leg. src-0005 remains an UNREVIEWED PREPRINT whose per-model numbers are permanently unreadable by this agent. open_question[1] -- a human-analyst baseline F1 for ATT&CK technique extraction -- is now in its EIGHTEENTH cycle merely listed, so 'hard, unsolved sub-task' has still never been anchored to a human reference point. Cycle 28 discovered a human baseline in src-0018 (41 minutes per report against about 3.3 minutes) but it is a THROUGHPUT baseline, not an accuracy baseline, and it does NOT discharge that question; nobody may treat it as if it did. WHAT RESTORES A 3, concretely and cheaply: a T3 executing ctr-0006's resolution path -- drop or qualitatively restate candidate 1's cross-task comparison, record the Micro/Macro ambiguity, and read stage3_ti_drafting/ttp/ in the src-0017 artefact via raw.githubusercontent.com, which would give ONE of the two comparands a stated correctness rule. That is close to a one-fetch job and it is the same read carry-forward [34] has wanted for seven cycles. THIS DEMOTION IS A POINTER TO NEEDED WORK, NOT A VERDICT THAT THE ISSUE IS WEAK -- the same framing cycle 26 used when it demoted attribution-confident-wrong-gap, and cycle 28's T3 vindicated that framing by acting on it and closing ctr-0002. G3 GATE ARITHMETIC, STATED SEPARATELY SO IT IS AUDITABLE. ctr-0006 is open against this issue, so the gate applies. Merit score on the evidence = 2. I applied the CEILING reading, verified at source this cycle at scripts/validate_state.py lines 144-156, which errors only when an issue with an open contradiction scores GREATER THAN scale_max - g3_contradiction_demotion = 3. Merit 2 is under the ceiling, so THE CEILING DID NOT BIND and the demotion is a merit judgement, NOT a gate artefact; a successor must not restore a 3 by arguing the gate was misapplied. Under the SUBTRACTION reading that prompts/t4_assess.md step 3 and config.yml line 35 both state, this issue would read 0 -- stamping an issue with two supported candidates with the rubric label 'no candidate resolutions'. Carry-forward [4], TWENTIETH cycle, still awaiting a human.

ioc-extraction-reliability.rationale: HELD AT 2. This cycle adds a THIRD open contradiction against this issue without changing its merit, because my G2 landed on src-0008 -- one of this issue's four evidence ids, the stalest source in the base (last verified cycle 10), and a source whose own stored limitations section asked in terms for this pull before its numbers supported a scored resolution. ctr-0007 is the result. THE RULE THAT DECIDES THE SCORE IS UNCHANGED, and I re-checked it against the graph rather than against the previous rationale: level 3 requires the PRIMARY candidate to rest on at least two INDEPENDENT sources, and no candidate here meets it. Candidate 1 (LANCE 97.6% overall F1 against the manually-validated 1,791-IoC PRISM benchmark) rests on src-0003 alone. Candidate 2 (vanilla-LLM IoC precision 0.8240 GPT-4o / 0.8503 o3-mini / 0.8846 GPT-4o-FT / 0.6944 GPT-4o-mini-FT over 1,310 expert-annotated IoCs) rests on src-0007 alone. Candidate 4 cites [src-0003, src-0007, src-0017], but src-0017 is the SAME TEAM's artefact release for src-0007 and candidate 4's own text concedes it 'rests on ONE independent measurement plus arithmetic'. Three source ids is not three independent sources. That is the textbook definition of a 2. WHAT ctr-0007 ADDS, and it is the first new content on this issue since cycle 21. src-0008's stored claim that plain-text IoC recovery is near-free FOR CURRENT LLMS omits the fifth of five evaluated models. Verbatim from the paper's body text: 'ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini and Grok achieve 100% across all four phases without reporting uncertainties' -- and immediately after it -- 'Cohere, however, shows progressive degradation: 1% missed detections in P1, 2% in P2, 5% in P3, and in P4, 65% misses plus 35% explicit Don't Know responses'. Phases P1-P4 contain NO cryptography; Table 3 defines them as '1. Base64 encoding', '2. Identifier obfuscation', '3. Dead code injection', '4. Structural obfuscation'. Candidate 3 -- the SCAFFOLDING hypothesis, status proposed -- is the graph's only consumer of src-0008 and it consumes exactly the failing part, reading 'src-0008 finds an unscaffolded LLM recovers plaintext indicators ~100% of the time but is defeated entirely by encryption it has no tooling for'. Encryption is not the boundary for Cohere. I RECORD THAT THIS CUTS BOTH WAYS AND I ASSERT NEITHER DIRECTION: it defeats the tidy encryption-boundary illustration, and it arguably strengthens the scaffolding hypothesis itself, since regex pre-filtering and whitelisting would be largely indifferent to dead-code injection and control-flow flattening while a bare LLM evidently is not. Candidate 3 stays 'proposed' and a T4 has no standing to change it; the score does not move because candidate 3 never carried it. ALSO FROM THE SAME PULL, constraining every future use of src-0008. (1) It DEFINES ITS OWN METRICS TWICE, INCOMPATIBLY: body text 'Detection rate, i.e., the proportion of samples in which the model correctly identifies the presence of an IoC' against Table 6's caption 'DR reflects the detection rate, i.e., ratio of YES an answers. The Acc. reflects the percentage of correct detections among those positive answers.' A ratio of YES answers does not require correctness, so whether its 100% figure means 100% correctly identified or 100% answered YES is UNDETERMINED BY THE PAPER. That is the second source in this base to contradict itself on a metric definition, after src-0002's Micro-versus-Macro-F1. (2) The per-phase P0-P12 breakdown is IMAGE-LOCKED in Figure 2, confirmed by two fetches instructed to write CANNOT READ, so the stored 'roughly 0-1%' at P5-P6 and '~95%+ misses' at P7-P12 are FIGURE-DERIVED and not text-verified -- the FOURTH such instance in this base after src-0003, src-0005 and src-0018. What the body text supports is qualitative only: 'near-complete failure', 'encrypted IoCs become effectively opaque', 'once the code is encrypted, detection of IoCs remains essentially zero for all models'. (3) Table 6 IS readable text and was never captured in twenty cycles -- aggregate detection rates Anthropic 38.5%, ChatGPT 38.6%, Gemini 38.5%, Grok 35%, Cohere 22.8%, over roughly 4,350 queries each -- and it must never be quoted as a per-phase result. What PASSED: Table 7's hallucination rates verified exactly for the first time (Anthropic 0.11, ChatGPT 0.23, Gemini 4.8, Grok 0, Cohere 0), the abstract re-verified word for word, and carry-forward [5]'s phase-label worry is DISCHARGED IN OUR FAVOUR without PDF access. RESIDUAL WEAKNESSES CARRIED FORWARD UNCHANGED, DO NOT LET THEM BE STRIPPED. (i) src-0003's 97.6% is a CLASSIFICATION score over a regex-extracted candidate set -- verbatim, 'We assume a total of 1,789 candidate indicators, extracted using IoC Searcher, a state-of-the-art rule-based tool' and Figure 9's caption '... on IoC Classification' -- so it is not commensurable with src-0007's free-form extraction precision. (ii) src-0003 NEVER STATES ITS MATCHING RULE and that question is unresolvable from the sources in this base. (iii) src-0003's stored baseline figures (76% / 72% / 86%) are FIGURE-IMAGE-ONLY and must be cited as figure-derived. (iv) Per ctr-0004, src-0007's released IoC matcher is ONE-DIRECTIONAL substring containment, so its bias is ASYMMETRIC -- lenient toward short or fragmentary predictions, STRICT against verbose ones, which is the characteristic free-form-LLM failure mode -- and 'substring-permissive, inflates true positives' must never be repeated unqualified. WHAT THE ISSUE HAS ACHIEVED, so a held score is not misread as no progress: ctr-0001's METRIC confound is effectively eliminated (cycle 18's arithmetic that reconciliation by metric artefact alone would demand IoC recall of 0.09-0.15, plus src-0007's own Section 4.3 sentence calling IoC extraction 'relatively robust, although improvements in recall and processing efficiency remain necessary'), and src-0017 shows the omitted recall was a REPORTING choice since eval_ioc.py computes it in the same function as precision. Of ctr-0001's three confounds, METRIC is eliminated, SYSTEM has a paper-stated anchor in task format, and CORPUS is completely untouched and is now the largest gap. G3 GATE ARITHMETIC, STATED SEPARATELY, AND THIS IS THE EIGHTEENTH CYCLE THE SPECIFICATION DIVERGENCE HAS STAYED LATENT. Merit score on the evidence = 2. THREE open contradictions now sit on this issue (ctr-0001 cycle 9, ctr-0004 cycle 27, ctr-0007 cycle 29) -- the most any issue has carried. Under the CEILING reading, verified at scripts/validate_state.py lines 144-156 this cycle, the ceiling is 3 WHETHER THE GATE IS PER-ISSUE OR PER-CONTRADICTION, because a ceiling saturates; merit 2 is under it, so THE CEILING DID NOT BIND. Under the SUBTRACTION reading of prompts/t4_assess.md step 3, this issue reads 0 if the gate is per-issue and -6 floored to 0 if it is per-contradiction -- and NOBODY HAS SPECIFIED WHICH. That the two readings agree here only because the ceiling saturates is precisely why carry-forward [4] needs a human rather than another T4's opinion. All three contradictions stay open; a T4 has no standing to close any of them. WHAT WOULD ACTUALLY MOVE THIS SCORE: a second independent measurement of report-level IoC extraction, or a head-to-head on one corpus.

consistency-calibration-as-failure-mode.rationale: HELD AT 2, AND THE HANDOFF ASKED ME NOT TO SCORE ctr-0005 MECHANICALLY BUT TO SAY WHICH WAY I READ IT. I DID NOT APPLY ANY DEMOTION FOR ctr-0005, AND HERE IS THE REASONING IN FULL. ctr-0005's content is that this base was UNDER-citing src-0018, not over-citing it. The stored hedge -- 'NO NUMBER ON THE PAGE IS RECOVERABLE ... supplies ZERO citable magnitudes' -- was too broad, and it fenced off two things the page states in plain body text: a 41-minute-per-report human-analyst baseline against about 3.3 minutes, and, load-bearing for this issue, 'the LLM temperature parameter was set to 0 to minimize randomness and reduce non-deterministic behavior'. That is a STRENGTHENING of this issue's consistency leg: BOTH of its independent consistency sources now measure residual non-determinism UNDER a determinism setting -- src-0001 at temperature 0 with a fixed seed, src-0018 at temperature 0. The four PERFORMANCE artefacts remain unreadable images, confirmed a THIRD time, so the prohibition on quoting, estimating, ranking or comparing the consistency, abstention and extraction-performance magnitudes STANDS IN FULL. SO A CONTRADICTION ENTRY HERE IS NOT EVIDENCE THAT THE ISSUE IS WEAKER. Treating it as one would penalise an issue for a correction that improved it, and would create an incentive not to file such corrections at all -- which would be a direct attack on the mechanism G2 exists to run. I therefore score merit on the evidence and state the gate separately below. This is the live question carry-forward [41] raises and this is a T4's answer to it, recorded for whoever eventually decides carry-forward [4]: the G3 gate should distinguish a contradiction that UNDERMINES a claim from one that CORRECTS AN OVER-BROAD HEDGE, and neither prompts/t4_assess.md nor scripts/validate_state.py does. As it happens the ceiling reading makes the question moot at this score, which is a third independent reason the ceiling reading keeps working where subtraction would not. WHY IT IS STILL 2, AND THE REASON IS UNTOUCHED BY ctr-0005 BECAUSE IT WAS NEVER ABOUT LEG STRENGTH ON CONSISTENCY. This issue's title asks TWO things -- are CTI outputs consistent across repeated queries, AND are they well-calibrated in stated confidence -- and the evidence is ASYMMETRIC across those conjuncts. The candidate that answers BOTH is candidate 2, evidence [src-0001] alone: single-source, gpt4o only, nine table rows, and additionally the carrier of the gloss that ctr-0003 disputes. The candidate with two independent sources is candidate 5 (evidence [src-0001, src-0018]), and it answers only the CONSISTENCY conjunct and says so in its own terms. Independence there is clean -- no shared author, academia against industry lab, disjoint model sets a generation apart, no citation -- and it clears the cycle-16 scope ruling on that ruling's own terms because src-0018 is CTI proper. But declaring the half-answer primary in order to reach a 3 would be scoring the issue for a question it does not ask. Level 3 requires the PRIMARY candidate to have two independent sources; it does not. TWO FURTHER DISCOUNTS, both unchanged. (a) src-0018 SUPPLIES NO CONSISTENCY MAGNITUDE, so its corroboration is of DIRECTION AND EXISTENCE only and nothing may be compared against src-0001's CI widths (max 0.02 extraction against 0.06 generation). (b) src-0018's abstention metrics (FDR/FNR over an explicit None class) are a RESTRAINT construct, not ECE or Brier, and must never be pooled with proper-scoring calibration -- the same non-pooling rule already recorded for src-0015. ctr-0003 IS STILL OPEN AND STILL UNREPAIRED; cycle 28's T3 went to attribution-confident-wrong-gap instead, which was a defensible choice but leaves this issue where cycle 26 left it. Its content stands: src-0001's Table 6 was pulled whole (caption verbatim 'ECE and BS with gpt4o for information generation and extraction', nine rows where the base had stored five), every stored cell is EXACT, but the stored gloss 'calibration markedly worse for information-generation than information-extraction' does NOT hold row-wise at zero-shot -- generation goals 0.13, CVE 0.15 and country 0.19 all beat extraction campaign 0.25 and CVE 0.28, and the gloss's own worked example (CVE generation 0.15) beats its extraction counterpart (0.28). What survives is a mean gap that is small at zero-shot (0.278 against 0.205) and large only after fine-tuning (0.538 against 0.295), driven by two fine-tuned generation rows, with all four means DERIVED BY THIS AGENT and not printed. So the single-source calibration leg is not merely thin; its headline framing is the thing under dispute. A T4 has no standing to repair it. THE FOUR CYCLE-15 SOURCES STILL CONTRIBUTE NOTHING TO THE SCORE, and cycle 16's scope ruling is endorsed rather than re-litigated: src-0013, src-0014, src-0015 and src-0016 each measure a security-ADJACENT task (secure code generation, CVE-code vulnerability detection, JavaScript SAST review, simulated incident response), none measures IoC extraction, TTP mapping, attribution or report drafting, and none tests a model from src-0001's, src-0002's or src-0005's lists. They establish that the MECHANISM is not one team's artefact, which is real and is held as context. If candidate 3 were ever promoted, one of its legs (src-0016) carries a known quotation defect found at cycle 21 -- a stored 'verbatim' quotation that splices a real sentence to a table cell. ALL SIX open_questions remain open. G3 GATE ARITHMETIC: ctr-0003 and ctr-0005 are BOTH open against this issue. Merit score on the evidence = 2. CEILING reading applied, verified at scripts/validate_state.py lines 144-156 this cycle: ceiling = scale_max - g3_contradiction_demotion = 3, and it is 3 whether the gate is per-issue or per-contradiction because a ceiling saturates; merit 2 is under it, so THE CEILING DID NOT BIND. Under the subtraction reading this reads 0 or -4 floored to 0 depending on a choice nobody has specified. WHAT WOULD MAKE THIS A 3, concretely: a T3 executing ctr-0003's resolution path (rewrite candidates 1 and 2 to the mean-and-fine-tuning version, close the entry, designate a primary candidate that actually covers both conjuncts) and ctr-0005's (state the temperature-0 protocol, correct the scope of the image prohibition, and decide whether the 41-minute human baseline belongs in this issue at all -- it is a THROUGHPUT fact, not a reliability fact, and must not be smuggled into a reliability claim). CARRY-FORWARD [37] IS ENDORSED AND STRENGTHENED AGAIN: the two conjuncts are legs of visibly different and now diverging strength, only a T2 can split them, and the next T2 is cycle 44 at the earliest. Split, the consistency child would plausibly score 3 and the calibration child 2; unsplit, the title binds them and the weaker leg governs.

attribution-confident-wrong-gap.rationale: HELD AT 2, WITH THE G3 CEILING NOW LIFTED FROM 3 TO 5 AND DELIBERATELY NOT USED. ctr-0002 is RESOLVED (resolved_cycle 28), so this issue carries NO open contradiction and nothing caps it. That is a LIFTED CONSTRAINT, NOT AN ARGUMENT FOR A SCORE. Cycle 26 recorded its 3 -> 2 demotion as a MERIT judgement explicitly not a gate artefact, with the instruction that a successor must not restore a 3 by arguing the gate was misapplied; I honour that, and note the arithmetic makes it easy to honour -- the ceiling never bound at 2 in the first place, so lifting it changes nothing. Cycle 26 also wrote that adopting ctr-0002's reading (a) 'returns this issue to 3 immediately and I would expect it to'. Cycle 28 deliberately declined to use that as a reason and so do I: a prior T4's expectation is not a finding. I SCORED THE GRAPH AS CYCLE 28 LEFT IT, reading all three candidate_resolutions and all three open_questions in full rather than any rationale's account of them. THE EVIDENTIAL POSITION MOVED IN BOTH DIRECTIONS AND I WEIGH BOTH. GAINED: THE PRIMARY CANDIDATE IS REWRITTEN AND IS NOW HONEST. The 86-versus-52 framing is RETIRED BY NAME inside the candidate's own text -- CTIBench defines Plausible Accuracy as 'the fraction of correct and plausible answers combined', so it CONTAINS Correct Accuracy and the inequality was true by construction and evidenced nothing. It is replaced by the paper's own hallucination-inclusive third bucket, defined verbatim as 'incorrect answer (when the LLM misattributes the threat actor due to misjudgment, hallucination, or spurious correlation)', numerically equal to 100 minus Plausible Accuracy: GPT-4-turbo 14%, GPT-3.5-turbo 38%, Gemini-1.5 26%, LLAMA3-70B 20%, LLAMA3-8B 64%, over 50 real threat reports, with the authors stating that they 'manually verify each LLM response to account for the multiple aliases that threat actors often use'. THOSE FIVE VALUES ARE DERIVED BY SUBTRACTION FROM TABLE 1 BY THIS AGENT AND ARE NOT PRINTED ANYWHERE IN THE PAPER; the candidate says so in its own text and this rationale says so too, as required. Every cell they are derived from is exact across three fetches (cycles 23 and 28). Outright misattribution running from roughly one report in seven for the best model to nearly two in three for the weakest, on real alias-tolerant material, is a real finding and a considerably better one than the artefact it replaced. LOST: src-0004 WAS REMOVED FROM THAT CANDIDATE'S EVIDENCE, on a reason internal to src-0002's own scoring rule. open_question[2] was ANSWERED at cycle 28 after ten cycles merely articulated: CTI-TAA's correct bucket is defined as 'when the LLM accurately identifies the threat actor or one of its aliases', APT29 and Midnight Blizzard are two names for one group, and the ENISA passage named the RIGHT group while misstating which vendor uses which name -- so the ENISA defect is a naming/citation-fabrication sub-type that is INVISIBLE TO THE INSTRUMENT this issue's quantified leg rests on, and under CTI-TAA's own rule the ENISA sentence would score CORRECT. Its evidential home is institutional-incident-real-world-impact. This issue's central claim therefore LOST ITS SECOND SOURCE, and that loss is larger than the gain from the rewrite. AND THE DECISIVE FINDING, entered at cycle 28 as a new supported candidate so that the graph carries it: NO SOURCE IN THIS KNOWLEDGE BASE MEASURES EXPRESSED CONFIDENCE ON THREAT-ACTOR ATTRIBUTION AT ALL. src-0002 partitions outputs by correctness only and defines no confidence construct anywhere in its metric section; src-0007's 'Content: Threat Actor' block is an LLM-judged 1-5 QUALITY rubric that grades how good an attribution is, not how confidently it is asserted; src-0004 attaches no measurement of any kind; and the base's only confidence measurements -- src-0001's and src-0013's ECE and Brier scores -- are on different task sets entirely and belong to consistency-calibration-as-failure-mode, which this issue already lists in depends_on. So THE ISSUE'S TITULAR QUANTITY IS UNMEASURED BY EVERY SOURCE IT CITES. HOW I SCORED THAT, since the handoff asked and the rubric does not distinguish an UNMEASURED question from a NEGATIVELY ANSWERED one. The rubric scores the evidential state of an issue's candidate_resolutions, so I applied it to the candidates rather than to the title. Candidate 1 is a supported resolution of the ERROR-RATE sub-question resting on src-0002 ALONE, corroborated in direction only by candidate 3, which is deliberately 'proposed' because src-0007's Table 4 is still a single unreplicated pull from cycle 15 and its GPT-4o (FT) column is suspect. One supported candidate with single-source support is exactly the rubric's definition of a 2. I CONSIDERED 3 AND REJECTED IT: the only candidate citing more than one source is the SURVEY candidate, and its three ids are not three sources corroborating a resolution -- each is cited for what it LACKS, which makes it one agent's audit of the base rather than independent measurement. Counting it as two-independent-source support would award a 3 for the finding that nobody has measured the thing, which is exactly the kind of mechanical count step 5 warns against. I ALSO CONSIDERED 1 AND REJECTED IT: a supported candidate does exist, and 1 means none does. TWO ITEMS CARRIED UNCHANGED. src-0007's GPT-4o (FT) column reads 3.964 / 3.655 / 2.967 against o3-mini's 3.964 / 3.656 / 2.968, tracking to within 0.001 on all six rubric rows across two independent pulls -- as-printed, not a fetch artefact, cause unknown, do not guess -- so any claim resting on that column must say the column is suspect. And the rubric's ABSOLUTE level is uninterpretable (1.140 out of 5 normalises to 0.228 or 0.035 depending on x/5 versus (x-1)/4, a normalisation the paper never states), so ONLY within-table contrasts may be cited -- the load-bearing one being that the same GPT-4o scores 3.686 / 3.458 / 3.612 on 'Content: Root Cause' in the same table, making 1.140 an attribution-specific deficit rather than a general inability to draft. G3: no contradiction is open against this issue, so no adjustment applies. This is the ONLY issue in the graph in that position other than the four never contradicted at all. CARRY-FORWARD [45] IS ENDORSED: this issue bundles a well-evidenced attribution-ERROR-RATE question with an attribution-CONFIDENCE question that has no evidence at all, only a T2 can split it, and the next T2 is cycle 44 at the earliest. Until then the title binds the two and the weaker leg governs -- which is the same structural fact holding consistency-calibration-as-failure-mode at 2, and I am scoring both issues consistently for it rather than treating one as unlucky. WHAT WOULD MOVE THIS SCORE: any source that partitions post-2024 attribution outputs into correct / underdetermined-but-related / outright-wrong, or that measures verbalised confidence on attribution. open_question[0] names this as the highest-value collection target for the issue; the next T1 is cycle 43, so the realistic route is a T3 with search budget. The cheapest untried lead for open_question[1] is CTIBench's own released dataset or evaluation artefact, which would carry per-report ground truth -- the same route that worked for src-0007 at cycle 21.

task-dependent-reliability-framing.rationale: HELD AT 3. The counterargument that keeps it off 4 got stronger again this cycle without crossing the line that would drop it to 2, and I state both movements. Nothing has touched this issue since cycle 16 (attempts [6, 16]). THE LEVEL-3 BAR IS CLEARED BY LEGS THAT ARE IMMUNE TO THE OBJECTION, which is the whole reason this is 3 and not 2: src-0007's rubric contrast (Content: Threat Actor 1.140 against Content: Root Cause 3.612) is measured on ONE instrument within ONE table, and src-0006's nine rows are all F1 on one corpus and one model set. The qualitative claim that measured CTI reliability varies sharply by sub-task is not in doubt, and candidates 1 and 2 together rest on seven distinct sources from at least five unaffiliated teams. WHY IT IS NOT BACK TO 4, unchanged in substance and now anchored on BOTH sides of the comparison rather than one. Cycle 22 lowered it from 4 for a counterargument the issue does not state anywhere: a within-study design holds team, corpus, models and harness constant but DOES NOT HOLD THE SCORING RULE CONSTANT, and a cross-sub-task score spread is a task-difficulty fact only if the sub-tasks are scored comparably. The issue text still does not mention the problem, and an issue cannot be credited with addressing an objection it has not noticed. Known instances now number FOUR: (i) src-0017 and ctr-0004 -- src-0007's released IoC matcher is ONE-DIRECTIONAL substring containment, any(pred.lower() in gt.lower() for gt in gt_set), and its ATT&CK and rubric scorers have never been read; (ii) src-0003 -- the 97.6% is a classification score over a regex-extracted candidate set; (iii) src-0005 -- multi-select multiple choice, metric verbatim 'the share of questions for which the system selects all correct options and only the correct options', questions generated by Llama 3.2 90B and Llama 4 Maverick with an author-acknowledged contamination risk; and (iv) NEW THIS CYCLE, from ctr-0006, the CTIBench side -- src-0002 defines CTI-MCQ and CTI-RCM as multi-class classification accuracy against a multi-label F1 over 397 techniques, never states an ATT&CK correctness rule, and CONTRADICTS ITSELF on whether that F1 is Micro or Macro ('We adopt the Micro-F1 score as the evaluation metric for the CTI-ATE task' against Table 1's header 'CTI-ATE (Macro-F1)'). So FOUR of the eight sources in this issue's evidence list are now known to score their tasks in mutually non-comparable ways. ONE MORE INSTANCE FROM MY OWN G2, recorded although src-0008 is not in this issue's evidence list and it changes nothing here: src-0008 defines 'detection rate' one way in its body ('the proportion of samples in which the model correctly identifies the presence of an IoC') and another in Table 6's caption ('ratio of YES an answers'). That is the second source in this base to contradict itself on a metric definition. The pattern is now systemic enough that any cycle asserting a cross-task comparison in this project should treat the quantities as non-commensurable until the scoring rules have actually been read. WHAT RESTORES 4, unchanged, cheap, and now more valuable than when it was written: read stage3_ti_drafting/ttp/ in the src-0017 artefact via raw.githubusercontent.com and src-0006's per-task scoring definitions, then STATE AND ANSWER the objection in the issue text. If the scoring rules turn out comparable, cycle 19's argument stands as written and the 4 is correct. NOT ALL LEGS ARE AFFECTED, WHICH IS WHY THIS IS NOT A 2: src-0007's within-instrument rubric contrast is immune, and src-0006's nine rows are all one statistic on one corpus and model set. The claim remains supported; it is the ROBUSTNESS that fails. RESIDUAL WEAKNESSES CARRIED, DO NOT LET THEM BE STRIPPED: src-0013's leg of candidate 2 measures secure code generation, not CTI, and defers to the cycle-16 scope ruling; candidate 1's prose still contains superseded ordinal-axis language that the cycle-16 split moved out of this issue, and a future T2 or T3 should annotate rather than delete it; src-0003's stored baseline figures (76 / 72 / 86) are figure-image-only and must not be cited as reported values; src-0005 is an unreviewed preprint whose per-model numbers are permanently unreadable by this agent, and its 43-53% against 23-34% cross-task spread is NOT a controlled contrast (different corpora, different question-generation pipelines, different random baselines of about 1.7% against 0.63%); and per ctr-0003, a cycle citing src-0001 here must keep the consistency and calibration halves apart and must not carry the 'markedly worse' framing -- the consistency half (CI widths 0.02 against 0.06) is re-verified and stands. WHAT IS NOT A COUNTERARGUMENT, carried from cycles 19, 22 and 26 because the reasoning is still right: cycle 18's derivation that src-0006's mean between-MODEL range within a task (0.272) nearly equals the mean between-TASK range within a model (0.263) does not undercut this issue -- a mean between-task range of 0.263 within a single model, running to 0.404 for LL70, CONFIRMS that reliability varies by sub-task. What it undercuts is sub-task as the PRIVILEGED explanatory variable, which lives in the child issue. Three open_questions remain, so 5 was never in view. No open contradiction is filed against this issue, so no G3 adjustment applies -- but I record that ctr-0006 explicitly names this issue as exposed 'more weakly', and a T3 acting on ctr-0006 should check whether candidate 1's src-0002 leg needs the same restatement it prescribes for ttp-attack-mapping-reliability.

extraction-vs-reasoning-ordinal-axis.rationale: HELD AT 3. Nothing has touched this issue since cycle 18 (attempts [17, 18]) and no source in its evidence list changed this cycle. SCORED ON EVIDENTIAL STATE, NOT ON THE POLARITY OF THE ANSWER: the title question is answered in the NEGATIVE -- the proposed ordinal ranking is not supported -- and a supported negative answer is a supported resolution, since the rubric is definitional about whether a supported resolution EXISTS rather than about what it concludes. The primary candidate rests on two independent sources from unaffiliated teams, on different corpora with disjoint model sets, by two distinct routes. Route 1, src-0006's Table 2 restricted to its nine F1 rows: Contextualization-stage mean 0.636 against Attribution-stage mean 0.602, a gap of 0.034 that is in the predicted direction but is roughly one eighth of the 0.272 mean between-model spread on a single task, and the best-performing task in the whole subset is TTP Extraction at 0.673, an Attribution-stage task -- so the ordering is not merely weak, it is locally INVERTED at its strongest predicted point. Route 2, src-0007's Table 4, the source that appears to support the ordering, reverses its own middle-to-third rung between two models of the same family under both defensible normalisations. WHY ctr-0006 IS NEUTRAL-TO-FAVOURABLE HERE WHILE IT COST ttp-attack-mapping-reliability A POINT THIS CYCLE, and the asymmetry is principled rather than convenient. This issue's supported claim is EVIDENTIAL AND NEGATIVE: that the available commensurable measurement does not support the proposed ordering. Every new finding that cross-sub-task numbers are non-commensurable removes evidence FOR the ordering, so it cannot weaken a claim that the ordering is unsupported. I checked the reverse reading -- that route 1 is itself weakened, because src-0006's per-task scoring definitions have never been pulled and its 'commensurable measurement' may not be commensurable either -- and the outcome is unchanged: under that reading no commensurable measurement supporting the ordering exists either, so the negative claim survives both ways. The same treatment was applied to ctr-0003 at cycle 26 and to ctr-0004; src-0002 is not in this issue's evidence list (it appears only in the REJECTED first candidate), so nothing is recalculated. WHY 3 AND NOT 4. Level 4 needs counterarguments addressed, and the candidate states four material caveats of which only one is addressed. (a) src-0006 reports no confidence intervals, no seeds and no repeat runs, so the headline 0.034 carries NO uncertainty estimate -- stated, not addressed, and not addressable from any source in this base. (b) Four of the nine rows are strictly monotone decreasing across all eight general-purpose model columns in exactly the printed order; this one IS addressed, by a robustness check dropping all four, leaving 0.641 against 0.592, gap 0.049, same direction, same best task. (c) THE DECISIVE ONE: the fourth rung of the proposed ordering, open-ended GENERATION, is not represented in the commensurable subset at all, so the candidate refutes only part of a four-rung ordering and is SILENT on one quarter of the ordering named in this issue's own title. (d) per-task scoring rules within src-0006's nine F1 rows have never been pulled, so 'all in F1' establishes that the statistic is constant, not that the matching rules behind it are. Seven open_questions remain, two of them fundamental. WHY NOT 2, considered seriously for the THIRD cycle running and recorded again so the disagreement stays explicit rather than implicit. The honest case for 2 is that route 2 is DEFEATING rather than CONFIRMING evidence, which would leave src-0006 alone carrying the claim and make it single-source. I resolve to 3 on the same ground cycles 19, 22 and 26 did: for a claim whose content is explicitly evidential, showing that the strongest apparent supporting source self-destructs on its own printed table IS direct evidence for that claim, and the local inversion (TTP Extraction at 0.673 beating every Contextualization task) is a qualitative fact about a printed table that does not depend on the missing uncertainty estimate. Nothing this cycle bears on the question either way. A successor that takes the other view should drop it to 2 and say so plainly. THE THIRD CANDIDATE IS CORRECTLY 'proposed' AND CONTRIBUTES NOTHING: model identity as the replacement explanatory variable, resting on the between-model 0.272 against between-task 0.263 near-equality, which cycle 18 itself objects to on three grounds -- ranges are not variance components and are outlier-sensitive, the cross-source TTP comparison behind its corpus-identity limb is uncontrolled in at least four ways at once, and both figures come from one study's table. No open contradiction is filed against this issue, so no G3 adjustment applies.

institutional-incident-real-world-impact.rationale: HELD AT 3. Nothing has touched this issue directly since cycle 12 (attempts [12]), but something happened TO it at cycle 28 from outside, and the net effect is CONSOLIDATION rather than strengthening -- which I record because cycle 26 flagged the possibility and a successor could easily over-read it. THE EXISTENCE CLAIM is carried by candidate 2 (evidence [src-0009, src-0010, src-0004]): ENISA's OWN publication pages carrying verbatim revision notices against publication dates of 1 October 2025 and 6 November 2025, both revised 09 January 2026, corroborating report count, dates, defect type and correction date independently of the Der Spiegel/Heise chain that was previously the entire basis. And by candidate 3 (evidence [src-0012, src-0004]): a second named incident at a different institution type -- EY Canada, 16 of 27 references hallucinated per GPTZero, report withdrawn -- discovered by the identical route of an outside party clicking through footnotes. Two incidents at two institutions via two mutually independent investigations, plus the affected institution's own correction record, clears the level-3 bar and the cycle-13 reasoning that raised it from 2 stands unamended. WHAT CHANGED AT CYCLE 28, AND WHY IT DOES NOT RAISE THE SCORE. attribution-confident-wrong-gap's open_question[2] was answered, and the answer is that the ENISA APT29 / 'Midnight Blizzard' error is a NAMING and CITATION-FABRICATION sub-type rather than an attribution-judgement error -- because CTI-TAA scores 'the threat actor or one of its aliases' as correct, and ENISA named the RIGHT group while misstating which vendor uses which name. src-0004's evidential home is therefore HERE, and its fabrication content sits in the same family as src-0011's ghost citations and src-0012's EY footnotes; the same ENISA report's other documented defect is 26 of 492 incorrect footnotes, which is exactly that family. BUT src-0004 WAS ALREADY IN THIS ISSUE'S EVIDENCE AND IN THREE OF ITS FOUR SUPPORTED CANDIDATES, so no new source arrives, no candidate changes status, and no measurement is added. The reclassification tidies the graph and removes a leg from a neighbouring issue; it does not strengthen this one. I am explicitly NOT scoring this issue up for a finding made elsewhere. NOT RAISED TO 4, and both reasons are structural and unchanged. (a) THE BASE RATE IS UNMEASURED AND IS BLOCKED BY SCOPE, NOT BY EVIDENCE VOLUME. Two named incidents are two data points, not a rate, and open_question[0] asks for a rate across CTI publishers. src-0011 (GhostCite) is not that rate and its candidate is correctly 'proposed': it audits peer-reviewed conference papers, which have reviewers where CTI reports have none; it defines a ghost citation as one absent from any major academic database, largely inapplicable to CTI footnotes which are news and vendor URLs; it reports per-PAPER rates (1.01% of Security-venue papers containing at least one invalid citation) not comparable with src-0004's per-FOOTNOTE 26/492; and its own authors call it a conservative lower bound. Treating a second anecdote plus an adjacent-population audit as a resolved base rate remains the most likely error available on this issue and it is not being made. Note also that src-0011 contradicts itself in prose versus table (body text says NeurIPS exhibits 'the highest absolute count (391 papers)' while Table 3 gives 391 invalid citations across 308 papers), so any cycle quoting its counts must take them from Table 3's columns. (b) THE AI-CAUSATION LEG IS THE WEAKEST PART AND IT IS THE PART THE TOPIC IS ABOUT. For ENISA, AI attribution rests entirely on Der Spiegel via Heise (src-0004); ENISA's own pages assign no cause at all, spiegel.de is unreachable to this agent, and every outlet repeating the 26-of-492 figure cites Der Spiegel, which is repetition rather than corroboration. For EY the 72% AI figure is the output of GPTZero's own commercial AI-detection product, so the load-bearing element there is the manually-checkable citation count. What is robustly established is that FABRICATED CITATIONS reached production at two named institutions; that AI CAUSED them is well-supported for EY and reported-but-not-primary for ENISA. A PERMANENT LIMIT RATHER THAN A PENDING ITEM: the two ENISA v1.2 PDFs cannot be opened by this agent at all (no PDF text extraction exists on this runner), so 'ENISA never disclosed the AI use' is established at landing-page level and is UNVERIFIABLE at document level here. That leg cannot strengthen and no further budget should be spent on it. Three of five open_questions remain wholly or mostly open, and candidate 4 itself honestly concludes there is no single institutional response pattern to report -- an accurate non-answer on n=2, not a resolution. NO G3 ADJUSTMENT: no contradiction is filed against this issue, and cycle 12's reasoning for not opening one over ENISA's silence is endorsed -- the revision notices assign no cause at all, and silence is not a competing claim, so G3's 'two supported claims in conflict' test is not met. I applied the SAME test this cycle in declining to open a contradiction over src-0008's internal phase-label inconsistency, where the conflict is inside the source and our state records the majority reading; the consistency across cycles is deliberate. Best available route to a 4 remains GPTZero, which runs an automated pipeline over the right population and publishes findings one report at a time -- still the only lead any cycle has found that could produce a rate rather than another anecdote.

automated-triage-under-refusal.rationale: HELD AT 2. This issue still has attempts [] -- it is the only issue in the graph never worked on -- and nothing has touched it since cycle 21's Table 4 pull gave it evidence as a by-product. It has now lost FOUR consecutive selections, and per carry-forward [30] the mechanism is created_cycle, so the newest issue in a graph is structurally disadvantaged forever with no expiry. THE FORMAL READING WOULD GIVE 3 AND IT IS STILL WRONG. The single candidate_resolution is at status 'supported' with evidence [src-0007, src-0015], which on a mechanical count is two independent sources on the primary candidate. The state itself forbids that count: src-0015's own index entry records it as THE WEAKEST-PROVENANCE SOURCE IN THIS BASE and says in terms that it must not be the sole support for any candidate_resolution -- single-author preprint filed cs.AI with no stated venue, peer review or affiliation; n = 40 synthetic RL-seed episodes per model from a 60-seed pool with no confidence intervals, so only the GPT-5.2-versus-Sonnet-4.5 contrast is robust and the middle two models' ordering is unresolved. The candidate itself agrees, stating that the claim RESTS on src-0007 and that src-0015 'is worth little as independent quantification'. Two sources of very unequal quality must not read as two independent confirmations, so what this issue has is one load-bearing source plus a directional corroborator: a 2 by the rubric's definition of partial evidencing. WHAT IS SOLID, and it is table-verified rather than summary-derived since cycle 21: src-0007's triage precision/recall asymmetry holds as stated -- across both triage tasks and all four models, precision (Accepted) spans 0.2717-0.3982 and recall (Accepted) spans 0.9091-1.0000. Fine-tuning does not fix the asymmetry and on the Article task WORSENS precision (GPT-4o 0.3037 to GPT-4o FT 0.2717 with recall unchanged at 0.9798-1.0000), the same direction as src-0001's fine-tuning finding and cycle 16's ATT&CK finding. ONE CAVEAT ADDED SINCE THIS ISSUE WAS LAST SCORED, from ctr-0004: src-0007's released IoC matcher is one-directional substring containment and its TRIAGE scorer has never been read either, so these figures inherit the same unread-scorer gap that carry-forward [34] identifies across this base. THE DECISIVE REASON THIS IS NOT 3 REMAINS: the issue's title question is not answered by its own supported candidate. open_questions[0] asks whether over-acceptance is a property of the MODELS or of the HARNESS, and neither source varies the decision threshold, the stated cost of a false positive, the availability of an explicit abstain option, or the presence of a human confirmation step. The issue text concedes that until that experiment is run, 'the models under-refuse' and 'these harnesses were built with no refusal affordance' are INDISTINGUISHABLE. The harness explanation is not hypothetical: src-0003 established for a different sub-task that scaffolding can dominate measured reliability, src-0005's percentages are all-or-nothing multiple-choice accuracies whose difficulty is set by the option sets, and THIS CYCLE ADDS A FIFTH INSTANCE OF MEASUREMENT DESIGN DOMINATING A HEADLINE NUMBER -- src-0008's own metric definitions disagree with each other, body text 'the proportion of samples in which the model correctly identifies the presence of an IoC' against Table 6's caption 'ratio of YES an answers', so even a detection percentage can mean two different things inside one paper. All five open_questions are unaddressed, including whether any precision-recall frontier exists (nobody has published the precision these models reach at a recall of 0.7, so it is unknown whether this is a tuning problem or a capability problem) and what the operational cost actually is (src-0007's ground truth IS the human analyst's accept/reject decision, so by construction it carries no human error bar and cannot say whether human triage would score better on its own benchmark). AN UNENTERED OBSERVATION THAT BEARS DIRECTLY ON THE CENTRAL OPEN QUESTION, carried for the FOURTH cycle so it is not lost, and it is carry-forward [27]: src-0015's Table 1 has a Reward column that no cycle has entered in the graph (GPT-5.2 3.07, Sonnet 4.5 2.37, Gemini 3 2.61, DeepSeek 3.2 3.45), so THE MODEL THE PAPER CALLS BEST-CALIBRATED EARNS THE LOWEST REWARD and the two highest-containment models take the two highest rewards. That points at the harness rather than the models, which is precisely what open_questions[0] asks. Its caveats travel with it: the fetched material does not state the reward's composition, n = 40 per model with no CIs, and the association is not strictly monotone (DeepSeek outscores GPT-5.2 at lower containment). It concerns an ALREADY-COLLECTED source so no new citation is needed -- but a rationale is not the graph, and only a T3 targeting this issue can enter it. WHAT IS STILL ENTIRELY MISSING is the curl/HackerOne case -- the bug bounty ended 31 January 2026 after a flood of AI-generated reports, with roughly 20% of submissions AI slop by mid-2025 and the confirmed-vulnerability rate falling from about 15% to under 5%. It is currently an open_question on this issue and NOT evidence: no curl source exists in state/knowledge/index.json and G1 forbids inventing one. FIVE cycles have now judged it the highest-value uncollected source in the project and none has reached it; a T3 may add sources, so a T3 targeting this issue is the first realistic route. ONE POOLING ERROR TO AVOID, recorded at the candidate and repeated here: src-0015's 'calibration' is an action-threshold construct (false-positive rate, evidence-gating), NOT the ECE/Brier confidence calibration of src-0001 and src-0013, and the two must never be averaged or quoted as one measurement -- the same rule now also applies to src-0018's FDR/FNR abstention metrics. No open contradiction is filed against this issue, so no G3 adjustment applies.
